Name: AcadianPalmettoCypressShelter
Description: A primitive frontier cabin of split cypress logs, woven reed thatch, and bog moss chinking.

Name: AgateFlakingShrine
Description: A small stone altar of stacked petrified wood blocks surrounding a polished agate anvil stone for flintknapping.

Name: AncestralPitHouse
Description: A semi-subterranean shelter with excavated floor, sandstone retaining walls, and juniper post roof.

Name: AncientFossilizedLodge
Description: A substantial dwelling of heavy petrified wood trunks with agate-inlaid doorways and translucent chalcedony windows.

Name: AncientGreekStoneTheater
Description: A hillside semi-circular theater with tiered limestone seating and marble orchestra floor.

Name: AndenesAgriculturalTerrace
Description: A multi-layered agricultural terrace with dry-stone retaining walls and gravel drainage layers.

Name: ApacheLeapStronghold
Description: An imposing mountain fortress with granite masonry towers, heavy ironwood gates, and multi-level saguaro colonnades.

Name: AppalachianNotchCabin
Description: A classic pioneer log cabin of hand-hewn chestnut timbers joined with dovetail corner notches.

Name: ArthurianLimestoneKeepCastle
Description: A monumental stone stronghold with limestone curtain walls, iron-sheathed oak portcullises, and amber-inlaid throne room.

Name: ArthurianTimberMeadHall
Description: A grand chieftain's hall with heavy oak posts, thatched roof, iron hearth fixtures, and carved amber finials.

Name: BambooScreen
Description: A folding bamboo screen. Divides space, lets light through.

Name: BayouSmokehousePotager
Description: A cypress timber outbuilding with bog-iron hinges and clay-moss lining for curing meats, paired with a kitchen garden.

Name: BioluminescentPassage
Description: An underwater passage lit by bioluminescent algae in the walls, with cave pearl markers. The Vorticist color in living form — blue-green against black basalt.

Name: BitumenBakedBrickRampart
Description: A heavy city defense wall of mudbrick core encased in kiln-baked bricks set in bitumen mortar.

Name: BitumenSealedDomesticHouse
Description: A courtyard house of sun-dried mudbricks with bitumen waterproofing and reed-mat ceiling support.

Name: BoneChandelier
Description: A hanging chandelier of strung vertebrae and amber crystals, lit from within. O'Keeffe's skull against the sky, made into a light fixture.

Name: BoneCleaningStation
Description: A workbench with copper tools for cleaning bones — brushes, chisels, and wire. The meeting place between the bone and the keeper.

Name: BoneDisplayNiche
Description: A carved limestone shelf for displaying cleaned bones. The first act of preservation — giving the bone its own space, its own light.

Name: BousillageShotgunHouse
Description: A narrow single-story home on elevated cypress stilts with mud-and-moss bousillage wall infill.

Name: CarvedCookingHearth
Description: A fire pit carved into the cave floor with smoke channels cut upward through the stone. Amber crystals provide light, bone provides fuel.

Name: CarvedCouncilChamber
Description: A meeting hall carved from the rock, with gargoyle stone sentinels watching from the walls and glow moss lighting the chamber.

Name: CarvedSacredGrotto
Description: A sacred space carved deep into the rock, with gargoyle stone eyes watching, amber crystals casting warm light, and cave pearls adorning the altar.

Name: CarvedSandstoneHaveli
Description: A grand merchant courtyard residence with intricately carved sandstone jali screens and sandalwood doorways.

Name: CarvedSandstoneNiche
Description: A simple carved niche in the rose sandstone cliff. The Subtractive Family's extrovert — the carving is visible, decorative, announced.

Name: CarvedSleepingHollow
Description: A sleeping hollow carved directly from the rock, lined with cave mushroom padding. The bed is the negative space — the building is what you removed.

Name: CarvedStorageNiche
Description: Shelves carved into the cave wall, decorated with cave pearls. The Subtractive storage — the shelf is the absence of stone.

Name: CarvedThresholdNiche
Description: An entry chamber carved into limestone, lit by bioluminescent glow moss in wall niches. The first act of subtraction — removing stone to make a space.

Name: CatacombCubiculum
Description: A vaulted burial chamber with shadow moss insulation, bone displays, and gold-inlaid walls. The Klimt 'Death and Life' painting made into a room.

Name: CatacombNiche
Description: A burial niche built from ancient brick, lined with sound-absorbing shadow moss. The catacomb's first adequate resting place.

Name: CathedralOfStSophia
Description: A magnificent multi-domed cathedral with imported limestone masonry and gold-gilded cupolas.

Name: CelticHillfortRampart
Description: A fortified portal with heavy oak timber palisade, dry-stone limestone walls, and iron-strapped doors.

Name: CelticWattleThatchRoundhouse
Description: A traditional circular dwelling with oak timber frame, woven wattle, and steep thatched reed and heather roof.

Name: CeremonialKiva
Description: A circular subterranean chamber with stone bench seating, central hearth, sipapu floor niche, and turquoise accents.

Name: ChalcedonyTrailMarker
Description: A tall stone cairn of petrified wood slabs topped with a luminous chalcedony crystal reflecting desert sunlight.

Name: ClassicalStoaColonnade
Description: A covered public walkway with marble columns, limestone rear wall, and olive wood rafters with bronze trim.

Name: CliffAlcovePalace
Description: A multi-story masonry structure inside a massive sandstone cliff alcove, with juniper beams and turquoise mosaics.

Name: CoastalRedwoodPlankHouse
Description: A traditional rectangular coastal dwelling of massive hand-split redwood planks on stone footings.

Name: CraftingBench
Description: A workbench with iron clamps and a waxed surface. Where everything begins.

Name: CreoleGalleryPlantationHouse
Description: A spacious Creole residence with surrounding gallery porch, cypress siding, and hand-forged bog iron fasteners.

Name: DeirElMedinaCraftsmanDwelling
Description: A domestic residence with sandstone foundation walls, papyrus thatch roof, and forged copper fittings.

Name: DesertDryStoneWall
Description: A rugged terrace wall of interlocking granite stones without mortar, reinforced with ironwood posts.

Name: DesertGlassSunSanctuary
Description: An open-air solar chapel with sacred scarab altars inlaid with gold leaf and Libyan desert glass.

Name: EnclosedToxicCourtyard
Description: A walled courtyard of thorn vine and shadow wood, filled with nightshade and venom sac specimens. The Poison Garden's inner sanctum.

Name: FaeAltar
Description: An altar that glows from within. The Fae Kingdom's sacred architecture.

Name: FaeKingdomPortal
Description: The portal to the Fae Kingdom. Living wood, fae light, ancient bog oak, and tuned crystal. The gate between worlds.

Name: FernThatchedRidgeShelter
Description: A coastal lean-to of split redwood posts with heavy roof thatch woven from giant sword ferns.

Name: FrontierLogCabin
Description: A rugged wilderness homestead of notched lodgepole pine logs chinked with mud and geyser salt mortar.

Name: FrontierRootCellar
Description: A subterranean food storage bunker with fieldstone walls, chestnut framing, and oak plank trapdoor.

Name: GardenChhatriPavilion
Description: An elevated kiosk with carved sandstone pillars, stone cupola dome, copper spire, and indigo fresco accents.

Name: GardenPlanter
Description: Raised bed lined with willow and moss. Where things grow.

Name: GargoyleSentinelPost
Description: A guarded passage with gargoyle stone sentinels embedded in gold-veined brick walls. The eyes watch. The 64Hz Listener is present.

Name: GeodeGate
Description: A gate of crystal and resonance that opens into the geode's heart. Requires materials from every level of the Inn.

Name: GeyserThermalLodge
Description: A grand wilderness lodge with heavy timber joinery, geothermal salt-cured siding, and polished obsidian fireplaces.

Name: GlazedLapisGatewayTower
Description: A fortified entryway of kiln-baked bricks glazed with deep blue lapis lazuli pigments.

Name: GoldCappedSandstoneObelisk
Description: A monolithic four-sided sandstone obelisk on a limestone pedestal topped with gold-plated pyramidion.

Name: GoldVeinedPassage
Description: A passage with gold veins running through dark brick, insulated with shadow moss. The Klimt golden phase as architecture — gold on dark, luminous against shadow.

Name: GothicVaultPassage
Description: A vaulted corridor with shadow wood beams, iron supports, ghost crystal glow, and moss-damped acoustics. The gothic architecture of the deep city.

Name: GrandCreolePlantationManor
Description: An opulent two-story raised Creole mansion with colonnaded galleries, wrought iron balustrades, and honey-waxed finishes.

Name: GrandMarbleParthenonTemple
Description: A monumental peripteral temple with marble Doric colonnades, bronze clamps, and copper roof tiles.

Name: GrandMortuaryTempleComplex
Description: A grand multi-terraced funerary complex with limestone facings, carved sandstone colonnades, and gold sacred vessels.

Name: GreatForestCanopyLonghouse
Description: A monumental multi-family longhouse of ancient old-growth redwood with elevated boardwalks and fog-moss insulated roofs.

Name: GreatHouseCitadel
Description: A monumental multi-story Great House with core-and-veneer sandstone masonry, massive juniper vigas, and turquoise plazas.

Name: GreatSmokyHomestead
Description: An expansive mountain farmstead with chestnut log main house, oak timber barn, stone springhouse, and ginseng curing sheds.

Name: GreatSteppedZigguratTemple
Description: A monumental multi-tiered stepped pyramid with mudbrick core, baked brick sheath, and lapis lazuli high temple.

Name: HexagonalChamber
Description: A hexagonal living space carved around a basalt column cluster. The walls are the column faces. The chamber IS the geology.

Name: HighlandHeatherLongbowRange
Description: A dedicated archery training field with carved yew bow racks, heather target butts, and oak pavilion.

Name: IchuAlderStorageHut
Description: A basic shelter of woven reed thatch supported by Andean alder framework.

Name: ImperialDragonPavilion
Description: A grand royal pavilion with cinnabar lacquered columns, copper dragon ornaments, silk canopy, and jade plaques.

Name: ImperialSunUsnuPlatform
Description: A grand multi-tiered ceremonial platform with fine ashlar stone, gold leaf ornamentation, and imperial canopy.

Name: IncaQullqaStorehouse
Description: A stone-and-thatch granary on elevated slopes with ventilated gables to preserve grain.

Name: IronAgeBogIronSmeltery
Description: A bloomery furnace of limestone and clay to extract iron from bog ore, under a simple oak and thatched shelter.

Name: IronwoodShadeRamada
Description: An open-air shade structure with desert ironwood corner posts and flat thatched roof of saguaro cactus ribs.

Name: KallankaGreatHall
Description: A monumental rectangular hall with multiple trapezoidal doors, polished stone walls, and tall alder roof frame.

Name: KarnakHypostyleColumnedHall
Description: A monumental colonnaded sanctuary with massive sandstone columns shaped into papyrus-bud capitals.

Name: KievanBanya
Description: A sealed timber log sauna with stone hearth furnace for generating intense steam.

Name: KlimtGoldStudio
Description: A studio decorated with Klimt gold patterns — the alchemy of base material transformed into gold. The inventor's atelier at full power.

Name: LacquerCabinet
Description: Bamboo cabinet with lacquered finish and copper hinges. Eastern elegance.

Name: LimestoneMegaron
Description: A single-room rectangular hall with central hearth, olive wood pillars, and limestone foundations.

Name: LithicCrystalSanctum
Description: A breathtaking ceremonial temple of fossilized tree trunks with fire agate floor mosaics and central chalcedony altar.

Name: LodgepoleSweatLodge
Description: A domed ceremonial sauna of flexible lodgepole pine saplings banked with mineral-rich geyser salt.

Name: MandanEarthLodge
Description: A large dome-shaped timber-and-earth dwelling over four central posts, insulated with thick turf.

Name: MarbleColumn
Description: Fluted marble column with bronze cap and olive wood base. The classical touch.

Name: MarshlandReedMudhif
Description: A vaulted communal hall fashioned from bundled giant marsh reeds arched together and plastered with clay.

Name: MultiStoryBrickPagoda
Description: A towering octagonal Buddhist pagoda of fired bricks with bamboo scaffolding and gleaming copper spire finial.

Name: MycenaeanCyclopeanWall
Description: A massive fortification wall of unworked limestone boulders bound with sandstone and bronze pins.

Name: NabataeanTombFacade
Description: An ornate tomb facade carved into the cliff face, with copper and gold inlays. The Subtractive Family's public face — the extrovert who dresses for the audience.

Name: NagaraStyleStoneTemple
Description: A majestic northern-style Hindu temple with soaring curvilinear sandstone tower and copper kalasha spire.

Name: NorseThrone
Description: Carved yew throne with runestone inlays and amber settings. The seat of a jarl.

Name: OakWall
Description: A sturdy wall of oak planks sealed with resin. The basic building block.

Name: ObservatoryDome
Description: A dome of star iron and cosmic crystal. Opens to reveal the full sky. The astronomer's crown.

Name: OKeeffeSkullAltar
Description: A single skull against the window light, set on a gold-inlaid altar with fossil base and calcium crystal supports. O'Keeffe's vision made architecture.

Name: OrnateStaveChurch
Description: A monumental multi-tiered wooden cathedral with massive corner pine staves, carved dragon heads, and amber-inlaid altar.

Name: OssuaryWall
Description: A wall constructed from bones and fossils set in limestone mortar, with calcium crystal inlays. The Sedlec Ossuary approach — death made architectural.

Name: PacificCrestTotemLodge
Description: A prominent tribal lodge framed by heavy carved redwood heraldic posts depicting clan lineages.

Name: PapyrusSandstoneWorkerHut
Description: A modest shelter with woven papyrus reed matting anchored to rough sandstone rubble.

Name: PetrifiedWoodWallShrine
Description: A ceremonial wall panel of slab-cut petrified wood with geometric mosaic bands of polished agate and chalcedony.

Name: PineFloor
Description: Smooth pine flooring. Warm underfoot, fragrant.

Name: PlainsTipiFrame
Description: A conical tripod framework of peeled lodgepole pine timbers, pegged with carved obsidian stakes.

Name: PoisonGardenTrellis
Description: A trellis of thorn vine and shadow wood that grows nightshade. Beautiful and deadly.

Name: PoisonPlanter
Description: A raised planter for toxic plants, built from thorn vine with nightshade borders and venom sac fertilizer. The Gorey garden in miniature.

Name: PrivateWorkshop
Description: A personal crafting studio with shadow wood walls, undercity iron workbench, and ghost crystal accent lighting. The introvert's creative space.

Name: RaisedAcadianCottage
Description: A cozy elevated cottage on rot-resistant cypress piers with bousillage insulation and shaded gallery porch.

Name: RedwoodBarkSweatLodge
Description: A conical purification lodge of thick fibrous fallen redwood bark slabs chinked with damp coastal fog moss.

Name: ReedMat
Description: Woven reed mat. The simplest comfort — a dry place to sit.

Name: RoseSandstoneShelter
Description: A shelter carved into rose sandstone with copper fixtures. The O'Keeffe maximalism — the form made ornate to honor the material.

Name: RoundTable
Description: A great round table of English oak. No head, no foot. Equality made solid.

Name: RoyalSandstonePalaceChhatri
Description: An opulent palatial complex with domed chhatri pavilions, copper-sheathed spires, and sandalwood doors.

Name: SaltCrystalStorage
Description: A storage chamber built from basalt columns, lined with salt crystal. The salt preserves anything stored within. The Vorticist functional aesthetic.

Name: SandstonePuebloUnit
Description: An above-ground masonry room of hand-shaped sandstone blocks spanned by heavy juniper ceiling beams.

Name: ScholarsGardenStudio
Description: A private retreat with bamboo framing, silk window scrims, lacquered desks, and carved jade inlay.

Name: SeaGlassWindChime
Description: Strand of sea glass hung on copper wire. The tidal cave's decoration — the ocean's refuse made into art.

Name: SiheyuanCourtyardResidence
Description: A traditional four-sided courtyard home with grey fired-brick walls, bamboo roof rafters, and red lacquer doors.

Name: SonoranAdobeDwelling
Description: A sun-dried earth brick home on granite foundation, framed with ironwood lintels and saguaro rib ceiling joists.

Name: StainedWindow
Description: Desert glass set in gold and silver framing within sandstone. Light made sacred.

Name: StorageChest
Description: Water-resistant cypress chest sealed with amber. Keeps the damp out.

Name: SubterraneanStepwellPavilion
Description: A subterranean multi-story water reservoir with carved sandstone steps, teak bracing, and copper water-spouts.

Name: SuperstitionOutpost
Description: A fortified canyon refuge against granite cliffs with ironwood palisade walls and saguaro-rib ceilings.

Name: TeakSandalwoodTimberManor
Description: A traditional Southern Indian courtyard residence with teak joinery, sandalwood doors, and copper ridge caps.

Name: TerracedHangingGardenVault
Description: An elevated terraced vault with bitumen lining and reed mats to retain soil high above ground.

Name: TheBeethovenFriezeWall
Description: A narrative wall — gold patterns shifting to show scenes from the archaeological record. The dead remembering what they were. The frieze you walk alongside.

Name: TheCharnelCathedral
Description: The ultimate bone architecture — a cathedral where every surface is bone, every light is amber, every support is calcium crystal. The body's last structure made into the body's first monument.

Name: TheFinalRoom
Description: A simple room behind the Inn. A fire, a chair, a cup, a book. Built from one of everything. The seed the Inn grew from.

Name: TheGoldenCrypt
Description: The ultimate catacomb — gold-veined walls, gargoyle sentinels, bone displays, shadow moss silence, and ghost crystal memory. Death made beautiful. The earth holding you the way the tree holds the fire.

Name: TheGoreyGreenhouse
Description: A greenhouse of shadow wood and thorn vine, housing the Poison Garden's rarest specimens, lit by ghost crystal. The Gorey masterpiece — the macabre made beautiful, the dangerous made deliberate.

Name: TheInnFoundation
Description: The foundation of the Inn itself. Materials from every zone, every level, every biome. The building that builds all other buildings.

Name: TheInventorsAtelier
Description: The ultimate creative space — gold-vaulted ceilings, iron workbenches, shadow wood walls, ghost crystal memory, moss silence, and geode crystal focus. The room the child eventually built. The room that was THEIRS.

Name: TheMonastery
Description: The Subtractive Family's most adequate work — simpler than the Treasury, larger, higher in the mountains. The introvert's extrovert moment. The quiet building that is also the biggest.

Name: TheSubtractiveCathedral
Description: The ultimate subtractive architecture — a cathedral carved entirely from living rock, every column a removed space, every arch a negative, the building IS the geology.

Name: TheTidalForge
Description: A forge powered by the tidal vortex's mechanical force. Basalt construction, salt crystal tempering, sea glass observation, copper workings. The Vorticist machine.

Name: TheTreasury
Description: A monumental Hellenistic facade carved into rose sandstone, with copper detailing, gold urns, and desert glass skylights. The moment of revelation at the end of the Siq.

Name: TheVorticistCathedral
Description: The ultimate angular cave architecture — a cathedral of hexagonal chambers, sea glass windows, bioluminescent walls, and a central vortex. BLAST and BLESS in stone.

Name: ThornArchway
Description: An archway of living thorn vine with nightshade blooms. The Poison Garden's entrance — beautiful and dangerous, the Gorey aesthetic.

Name: TidalPoolShelter
Description: A shelter built from hexagonal basalt columns, insulated with tidal moss. Angular, functional, Vorticist. The cave's first adequate home.

Name: TorchHolder
Description: Iron bracket holding a beeswax torch. Lights the dark corridors.

Name: TraditionalSlavicIzba
Description: A cozy log cabin of horizontally stacked pine logs notched at corners, sealed with birch bark strips.

Name: TraditionalVikingLonghouse
Description: A bow-sided hall with heavy pine posts, wattle walls of birch, and insulated turf roof of moss and heather.

Name: TrelleborgRingFortPalisade
Description: A heavily reinforced timber rampart secured with iron bolts and anchored on cleaved runestone blocks.

Name: VikingAgeBoathouse
Description: A sturdy shoreline timber shed with open gable ends for storing longships over winter.

Name: VikingTurfPitHouse
Description: A simple semi-subterranean shelter insulated with birch bark, heather thatch, and damp bog moss turf.

Name: VikingVillageSmithy
Description: A stone-hearth forge under heavy timber frame, optimized for smelting bog ore into wrought iron.

Name: VortexObservationPlatform
Description: A platform overlooking the central vortex, built from basalt with sea glass railings and salt crystal supports. The Vorticist viewing point.

Name: WhiteningChamber
Description: A quiet chamber where bones slowly whiten in solution, lit by amber crystal. The last traces of organic color leaving, the structure becoming pure.

Name: WindAndRainCoveredBridge
Description: A sheltered river bridge with fired-brick piers and ornate bamboo roof pavilion sealed in lacquer.

Name: WoodenOnionDomedChapel
Description: A wooden church with stacked log walls, birch-shingle roofing, and an ornate helmet dome gilded with gold leaf.

Name: WoodlandLeanToShelter
Description: A three-sided forest shelter of split chestnut logs and bark roof tiles with ginseng drying racks.

Name: WoodlandsLonghouse
Description: A communal multi-family longhouse with arched chestnut sapling frames, oak bark shingling, and central hearths.

Name: WorkshopLampPost
Description: A lamp post for the Undercity's narrow streets. Undercity iron frame, shadow wood base. The crafted light of the inventor's city.

Name: WovenBambooSilkTeaHouse
Description: An airy roadside tea house with split-bamboo screens, silk wall hangings, and lacquered serving counters.

Name: Campfire
Description: A ring of stones holding fire — the first structure of any camp.
LoreConnection: Every forest site begins with a fire ring.

Name: StoneHearth
Description: A permanent fire pit of stone and mud — the heart of the campsite.
LoreConnection: Where the fire never goes out.

Name: Kiln
Description: A fired-clay chamber for baking ceramic — the potter's workshop.

Name: AdobeWall
Description: Mud and brick stacked into a perimeter — the campsite's first defense.
LoreConnection: The line between camp and wild.

Name: StoneCircle
Description: Sandstone standing stones arranged in a ring — the ancient gathering place.
LoreConnection: Where the old songs are sung.

Name: Watchtower
Description: A tower of sandstone and brick to watch the treeline — the grounds' eyes.
LoreConnection: Where the wolf is first seen.

Name: GlassFurnace
Description: A furnace of brick and sand for melting glass — the crystal-maker's fire.

Name: TheForge
Description: A brick forge with stone anvil — where ore is struck to the metal chord.
LoreConnection: 79 + 80 + 82 Hz — the chord of the Blacksmith's Forge.
